title: consistent-resizing-gesture-and-prefetching-for-large-grids
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Overview: This ticket designs a cohesive interaction pattern for large, virtualized table grids used across Redwood Console and the API usage dashboards. The focus is threefold: 1) consistent column-resize gestures with visual snap hints and keyboard accessibility; 2) buffered prefetching + overscan heuristics to smooth scroll and reduce jank for variable row heights; 3) a compact/comfortable/expanded density toggle that preserves visual alignment and keyboard navigation.

Problem statement: Several consumer-facing dashboards suffer from perceived jank when scrolling big datasets (1000+ rows) and inconsistent resize behavior across breakpoints. Engineering has instrumented spikes in frame-time and high GC pauses when the virtualization overscan is too small for dynamic row heights. Designers also discovered users struggle to resize narrow columns precisely on touch and trackpad because grab targets are inconsistent.

Goals:
- Define a single resizing interaction pattern that works for mouse, touch, and keyboard, with live preview and a snap-to-grid hint.
- Recommend overscan/prefetch defaults plus an adaptive strategy based on observed scroll velocity and row-height variance.
- Introduce density presets that don't break header alignment or selection affordances and are discoverable inside the table toolbar.
- Provide accessible keyboard flows for resize, column reordering, and density switching.

Constraints from engineering: The runtime uses continuous batching and a KV cache; increasing overscan increases memory and CPU cost. Dedicated customers expect latency SLOs which limit how many rows can be rendered synchronously. Any UI strategy must allow toggling to the previous behavior for debugging and comparison.

Proposed solution (summary):
- Resizing: Implement a 12px minimum grab boundary with a draggable handle that shows a light snap guide at 8px intervals. For touch, use an enlarged hit area and a short inertia preview. Keyboard: focus on header > press R to enter resize mode, arrow keys adjust width by 1px/5px (with alt modifier for 10px). Escape cancels. Enter commits.
- Buffered prefetching: Default overscan to 6 rows before/after the viewport for stable-height tables. For variable-height tables, use a reactive overscan that measures row-height variance over N samples and increases overscan to 12 when variance > 30%. Additionally, prefetch next chunk on fast scroll velocity (>1500 px/s) and render visually progressive placeholders to avoid layout shifts.
- Density modes: Add three presets (Compact, Regular, Relaxed) exposed in the table toolbar and persisted per-user. Switching should animate the row-height change over 120ms to maintain spatial continuity. Density should be keyboard reachable (T then D for toolbar, then arrows).

Acceptance criteria:
- Designers and eng agree on resize gestures and keyboard flows documented in the spec.
- Prototype (Figma + coded storybook) shows live-resize preview with snap hints and works for mouse/touch emulation.
- Measured reduction of scroll jank: 95th percentile frame time reduced by at least 20% on representative dashboard dataset (per perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood/company/tables-perf).
- Density presets toggle without misalignment; header cells remain aligned to body across all three presets in major browsers.
- Accessibility: screen-reader announces "Resize mode" and keyboard flows pass basic NVDA/VoiceOver manual checks.

Design artifacts and refs:
- Figma exploration (current working file): https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/tables-resize-prefetch
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/DS/Table+Resize+Prefetch+Spec
- Performance dashboard: https://dash.redwood/company/tables-perf
- Slack discussion thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234ABCD/p1675860000000

PRs and engineering links:
- Engineering spike branch: https://github.com/redwood/inference-ui/pull/8742
- Runtime perf experiment (ENG): ENG-22012

Decisions made:
- Use adaptive overscan (variance-based) over a fixed large overscan to balance memory and UI smoothness.
- Live-resize preview will be client-side only (no server roundtrips) and capped to avoid expensive reflows on very wide tables.
- Density presets persist in local user storage and can be overridden by account settings, to avoid forcing server config changes.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Increasing overscan reduces jank but increases memory; for Dedicated customers with tight budgets we expose a toggle in runtime settings (engineering to build). Follow-up: ENG-22078 to add telemetry for overscan memory impact.
- Touch drag smoothing improves UX but may make precise tiny adjustments harder; keyboard mode is provided for precision.
- Edge case: extremely tall rows (>2x normal) still cause spikes; plan a secondary strategy to virtualize by height-buckets if needed.
